name: IGA World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The promotion's top title, first decided in a round robin at its first pay-per-view, The Battle for Fort Knox, where Matt Allen beat Mark Davenport in the deciding match. Todd Bishop took it from Allen in a scaffold match at Requiem for Pain on 31 October 2001 and held it through the year's end.

name: IGA TV Championship
epitaph: A silver belt on a white strap, defended at least three times a month. Maxime St. Jean won the first title match, a six-man elimination at The Battle for Fort Knox, and held it through the rest of 2001.

name: IGA Jr. Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The promotion's title for wrestlers under 225 pounds, decided by a tournament in the autumn of 2001. Ryan Arnott was its first champion and kept it through a five-man ladder match at Devil's Night.

name: IGA Fight Club Championship
epitaph: A bronze belt on a red strap, defended anywhere but the arena: parking lots, bars and locker rooms. Malkav won it at the Last Chance Bar & Grille on Devil's Night, 30 October 2001.

name: IGA World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: White gold on a black strap with diamonds, the same design as the world title. Forever Unchained, Mark Davenport and Pandemonium, won the first tournament and defended the belts through the end of 2001.

name: IGA Euro Championship
epitaph: Introduced on 7 November 2001, when Estrago outlasted nine other men in an elimination match to become its first champion; he defended it against Nick Hart and Marco Avery.

name: IGA International Championship
epitaph: Created for a single night: a battle royal earned the shot, and Mark Davenport, already half of the IGA World Tag Team Championship, beat Donovan Keltrane for it after a rival promotion's wrestler ran in against the challenger.

name: IGA Women's Championship
epitaph: Held by Myranda "The Cat" Steele through every one of its own served defenses, against opponents from Sakuya Mistuhara and Alex Vale's own six-woman brawl to a solo challenge from Mizz Da Meaner.
